questions.q:
Statement I: A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha.
Statement II: The Rajya Sabha has the power to reject a Money Bill.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.exp: Money Bills originate only in the Lok Sabha; the Rajya Sabha can only make recommendations within 14 days and cannot reject them.

questions.q: Which city of Bihar is popularly known as the 'Silk City'?
questions.exp: Bhagalpur is famous for Tussar (Bhagalpuri) silk.

questions.q: Which is the national flower of India?
questions.exp: The lotus (Nelumbo nucifera) is India's national flower.

questions.q: The black soil of the Deccan plateau is best suited for which crop?
questions.exp: Regur (black) soil retains moisture and suits cotton, hence called 'black cotton soil'.

questions.q: Which Ashokan inscription describes the Kalinga war and Ashoka's remorse?
questions.exp: Rock Edict XIII records the bloody Kalinga war (261 BCE) and Ashoka's turn to dhamma.

questions.q: India's first satellite, Aryabhata, was launched in which year?
questions.exp: Aryabhata was launched on 19 April 1975 with Soviet help.

questions.q: The famous Sonepur cattle fair in Bihar is held near the confluence of which two rivers?
questions.exp: The Harihar Kshetra (Sonepur) fair is held at the Ganga-Gandak confluence in Saran district.

questions.q: Who is the author of the Hindi novel 'Godan'?
questions.exp: Godan (1936) by Munshi Premchand portrays the plight of a peasant, Hori.

questions.q: Who discovered penicillin in 1928?
questions.exp: Alexander Fleming noticed the antibacterial action of Penicillium mould in 1928.

questions.q: Which of the following was among the first recipients of the Bharat Ratna in 1954?
questions.exp: The 1954 awardees were C. Rajagopalachari, S. Radhakrishnan and C. V. Raman.

questions.q: National Youth Day in India is celebrated on the birth anniversary of
questions.exp: National Youth Day is observed on 12 January, Swami Vivekananda's birthday.

questions.q: How many Schedules does the Constitution of India contain at present?
questions.exp: The Constitution has 12 Schedules (the 12th, added in 1992, lists municipal functions).

questions.q: Who was the first Indian woman to win an individual Olympic medal?
questions.exp: Karnam Malleswari won weightlifting bronze at Sydney 2000.

questions.q: Who was the first Governor-General of independent India?
questions.exp: Mountbatten served from 15 August 1947 to June 1948, followed by C. Rajagopalachari.

questions.q: The national song of India, 'Vande Mataram', was composed by
questions.exp: Vande Mataram appeared in Bankim Chandra's novel Anandamath (1882); Tagore wrote the national anthem.

questions.q: Fundamental Rights are contained in which Part of the Indian Constitution?
questions.exp: Part III (Articles 12-35) contains Fundamental Rights.

questions.q: Which is the national animal of India?
questions.exp: The Bengal tiger (Panthera tigris) is India's national animal.

questions.q: The Human Development Index (HDI) is published by which organisation?
questions.exp: HDI, combining health, education and income indices, is published by the UN Development Programme.

questions.q: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre at Amritsar took place in
questions.exp: General Dyer ordered firing on 13 April 1919 (Baisakhi day).

questions.q: The river Gandak, which flows through Bihar, is also known as
questions.exp: The Gandak is called Narayani (or Saligrami) in Nepal.

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions?
questions.exp: The 73rd Amendment (1992) added Part IX and the 11th Schedule; the 74th dealt with urban local bodies.

questions.q: The Jnanpith Award is given for outstanding contribution in the field of
questions.exp: The Jnanpith Award is India's highest literary honour.

questions.q: Which vitamin is synthesised in human skin on exposure to sunlight?
questions.exp: UV-B rays convert 7-dehydrocholesterol in the skin into vitamin D3.

questions.q:
Match the battle with its year.
P. First Battle of Panipat   Q. Battle of Haldighati   R. Battle of Buxar
1. 1764   2. 1526   3. 1576
questions.exp: Panipat I was fought in 1526, Haldighati in 1576 and Buxar in 1764.

questions.q: The famous Nalanda Mahavihara is traditionally believed to have been founded by which Gupta ruler?
questions.exp: Nalanda was founded in the 5th century CE under Kumaragupta I; Dharmapala founded Vikramshila.

questions.q:
Statement I: Rajasthan is the largest Indian state by area.
Statement II: Goa is the smallest Indian state by area.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.exp: Rajasthan (about 3.42 lakh sq km) is the largest state and Goa the smallest by area; both statements are true.

questions.q: The writ of Habeas Corpus literally means
questions.exp: Habeas Corpus is issued to produce a detained person before a court to examine legality of detention.

questions.q: The tomb of Sher Shah Suri is located at which place in Bihar?
questions.exp: Sher Shah's tomb stands in the middle of a lake at Sasaram (Rohtas district).

questions.q:
Match the institution with its year of establishment.
P. Reserve Bank of India   Q. NABARD   R. Planning Commission
1. 1982   2. 1950   3. 1935
questions.exp: RBI was set up in 1935, NABARD in 1982 and the Planning Commission in 1950.

questions.q: Major Dhyan Chand, regarded as a legend of Indian sport, was associated with which game?
questions.exp: Dhyan Chand won three Olympic golds (1928, 1932, 1936) in hockey; his birthday is National Sports Day.

questions.q: Which modern city of Bihar was the ancient Mauryan capital Pataliputra?
questions.exp: Pataliputra, capital of the Magadha-Mauryan empire, is the modern city of Patna.

questions.q: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution?
questions.exp: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee; Rajendra Prasad presided over the Constituent Assembly.

questions.q: Which gas forms the largest percentage of Earth's atmosphere by volume?
questions.exp: Dry air contains about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen.

questions.q: Indian Standard Time is calculated on the basis of which longitude?
questions.exp: The standard meridian 82°30′ E passes near Mirzapur; IST is UTC+5:30.

questions.q: The Tropic of Cancer passes through how many Indian states?
questions.exp: It passes through Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram - 8 states.

questions.q: Bhikhari Thakur, known as the 'Shakespeare of Bhojpuri', is associated with which folk theatre form?
questions.exp: Bhikhari Thakur of Saran popularised Bidesia, a theatre form on the pain of migration.

questions.q: The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution were borrowed from the Constitution of
questions.exp: The Directive Principles were inspired by the Irish Constitution.

questions.q: National Science Day in India is celebrated every year on
questions.exp: It commemorates the discovery of the Raman Effect announced by C. V. Raman on 28 February 1928.

questions.q: The festival Chhath, widely celebrated in Bihar, is dedicated to which deity?
questions.exp: Chhath Puja is a four-day festival in which the Sun god Surya and Chhathi Maiya are worshipped.

questions.q: Who was the Governor-General of India at the time of the Revolt of 1857?
questions.exp: Lord Canning was Governor-General (1856-62) and became the first Viceroy in 1858.

questions.q: Which Indian city is popularly called the 'Pink City'?
questions.exp: Jaipur's old city was painted pink in 1876 to welcome the Prince of Wales.

questions.q: The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was fought between the Marathas and
questions.exp: The Marathas were defeated by Ahmad Shah Abdali's Afghan forces in 1761.

questions.q: Which river is called the 'Sorrow of Bihar' because of its frequent floods?
questions.exp: The Kosi shifts its course often and causes recurrent floods in north Bihar.

questions.q: Who is the author of the book 'The Discovery of India'?
questions.exp: Nehru wrote it in Ahmednagar Fort prison in 1944.

questions.q: Who is regarded as the 'Father of the Green Revolution in India'?
questions.exp: M. S. Swaminathan led high-yielding wheat and rice programmes; Kurien was the father of the White Revolution.

questions.q: The Western Ghats are also known as the
questions.exp: In Maharashtra, the Western Ghats are called the Sahyadri range.

questions.q: Mining, fishing and agriculture belong to which sector of the economy?
questions.exp: The primary sector extracts natural resources directly from nature.

questions.q: Dr. Rajendra Prasad, the first President of India, was born at Ziradei in which present-day Bihar district?
questions.exp: Ziradei is a village in Siwan district.

questions.q: Who founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828?
questions.exp: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha (Brahmo Samaj) in Calcutta in 1828.

questions.q: The Doctrine of Lapse was introduced by which Governor-General?
questions.exp: Dalhousie (1848-56) annexed states such as Satara, Jhansi and Nagpur by the Doctrine of Lapse.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a Himalayan range?
questions.exp: The Aravallis are an old fold-mountain range in Rajasthan; Himadri, Himachal and Shiwalik are Himalayan ranges.

questions.q: Who was the first Indian to win an individual Olympic gold medal?
questions.exp: Abhinav Bindra won gold in 10 m air rifle at the 2008 Beijing Olympics.

questions.q: Under which Article can the President proclaim a National Emergency?
questions.exp: Article 352 deals with emergency due to war, external aggression or armed rebellion; 356 is State Emergency, 360 Financial Emergency.

questions.q: Which of the following is a Kharif crop?
questions.exp: Kharif crops are sown with the monsoon (June-July), e.g. paddy, maize; wheat, gram and mustard are Rabi crops.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Sea water boils at a slightly higher temperature than pure water.
Reason (R): Dissolved salts raise the boiling point of a liquid.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: Dissolved solutes lower vapour pressure and cause elevation of boiling point, so A is true and explained by R.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the Election Commission of India?
questions.exp: Article 324 vests superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission.

questions.q: Which Gupta ruler is called the 'Napoleon of India' by V. A. Smith?
questions.exp: Samudragupta's many conquests, recorded in the Allahabad Pillar inscription, earned him the title.

questions.q: The financial year in India runs from
questions.exp: India's financial year starts on 1 April and ends on 31 March.

questions.q: The Quit India Movement was launched on 8 August 1942 from which place?
questions.exp: The AICC passed the Quit India resolution at Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay.

questions.q: What is the state bird of Bihar?
questions.exp: The house sparrow was declared the state bird of Bihar.

questions.q: The Jog Falls, one of the highest waterfalls of India, is formed by which river?
questions.exp: The Sharavathi river plunges down the Western Ghats in Karnataka to form Jog Falls.

questions.q: The Kesaria stupa, one of the largest Buddhist stupas in the world, is located in which district of Bihar?
questions.exp: Kesaria Stupa is in East Champaran (Purvi Champaran) district.

questions.q: Who appoints the Governor of a state in India?
questions.exp: Under Article 155, the Governor is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.

questions.q: Which state is the largest producer of tea in India?
questions.exp: Assam produces more than half of India's tea.

questions.q: The Sundarbans mangrove delta, home of the Royal Bengal Tiger, lies mainly in which Indian state?
questions.exp: The Indian Sundarbans in the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta lie in West Bengal.

questions.q: Which of the following is a direct tax?
questions.exp: A direct tax is borne by the person on whom it is levied, e.g. income tax; GST and duties are indirect.

questions.q: Who presided over the first session of the Indian National Congress held in Bombay in 1885?
questions.exp: The first INC session (1885, Bombay) was presided over by W. C. Bonnerjee; A. O. Hume was its founder-organiser.

questions.q: The Thomas Cup is associated with which sport?
questions.exp: The Thomas Cup is the world men's team championship in badminton.

questions.q: Madhubani painting is a traditional folk art of which region of Bihar?
questions.exp: Madhubani (Mithila) painting originated in the Mithila region of north Bihar.

questions.q: The ancient treatise on statecraft 'Arthashastra' was written by
questions.exp: Kautilya (Chanakya), minister of Chandragupta Maurya, wrote the Arthashastra.

questions.q: Chilika Lake, the largest brackish-water lagoon in India, is located in which state?
questions.exp: Chilika Lake lies on the coast of Odisha along the Bay of Bengal.

questions.q: Vikramshila Mahavihara, an ancient centre of learning in Bihar, was established by which Pala king?
questions.exp: Dharmapala (late 8th century) founded Vikramshila near Bhagalpur.

questions.q: Who administers the oath of office to the President of India?
questions.exp: Under Article 60, the oath is administered by the Chief Justice of India or the senior-most judge available.

questions.q: Indira Point, the southernmost point of India, is located in
questions.exp: Indira Point (6°45'N) is in Great Nicobar Island of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

questions.q: International Yoga Day is observed on
questions.exp: The UN General Assembly declared 21 June as International Day of Yoga in 2014.

questions.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution abolishes untouchability?
questions.exp: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form.

questions.q: What is the minimum age required to be elected as the President of India?
questions.exp: Article 58 requires a candidate to have completed 35 years of age.

questions.q: At which place did Gautama Buddha attain enlightenment?
questions.exp: Siddhartha attained enlightenment under the Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya in Bihar.

questions.q: The river Brahmaputra is known by which name in Tibet?
questions.exp: The Brahmaputra is the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet, Dihang in Arunachal Pradesh and Jamuna in Bangladesh.

questions.q: Which Mughal emperor built the Red Fort at Delhi?
questions.exp: Shah Jahan built the Red Fort (Lal Qila) when he shifted the capital to Shahjahanabad (1639-48).

questions.q: The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 was launched against which system?
questions.exp: Gandhi's first satyagraha in India was for peasants forced to grow indigo on 3/20 of their land.

questions.q: The Battle of Plassey, which laid the foundation of British rule in India, was fought in
questions.exp: The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 between Robert Clive and Siraj-ud-Daulah.

questions.q: Which is the longest river that flows entirely within India?
questions.exp: The Ganga (about 2,525 km) is the longest river wholly in India; Brahmaputra and Indus rise outside India.

questions.q: Which pass connects Srinagar with Leh?
questions.exp: Zoji La, in the Pir Panjal/Himalaya region, links Srinagar and Leh on NH-1.

questions.q: Who founded the Mauryan Empire in 322 BCE with the help of Kautilya?
questions.exp: Chandragupta Maurya overthrew the Nandas and founded the Maurya empire with Chanakya's guidance.

questions.q: Which is the highest peak lying entirely within India?
questions.exp: Kanchenjunga (8,586 m) is the highest peak in India; K2 and Everest are not wholly in India.

questions.q: Bihar was separated from the Bengal Presidency and formed into a separate province in
questions.exp: Bihar and Orissa became a separate province in 1912; Bihar and Orissa were split in 1936.

questions.q: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.exp: Under Article 89, the Vice-President is ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

questions.q: Which Indian state has the longest coastline?
questions.exp: Gujarat has the longest mainland coastline (about 1,600 km), followed by Andhra Pradesh.

questions.q: India's first lunar probe, Chandrayaan-1, was launched in
questions.exp: Chandrayaan-1 was launched by PSLV-C11 on 22 October 2008.

questions.q: Which part of the human eye controls the amount of light entering it?
questions.exp: The iris adjusts the size of the pupil and hence the amount of light entering the eye.

questions.q: What is the term of a member of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.exp: Rajya Sabha is a permanent house; each member serves a six-year term, with one-third retiring every two years.

questions.q: Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by which Amendment?
questions.exp: The 42nd Amendment (1976), on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation, added Part IV-A.

questions.q: The slogan 'Do or Die' was given by which leader during the Quit India Movement of 1942?
questions.exp: Gandhi gave the call 'Do or Die' at Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay, on 8 August 1942.

questions.q:
Match the organisation/movement with its founder.
P. Servants of India Society   Q. Swaraj Party   R. Satyashodhak Samaj
1. G. K. Gokhale   2. C. R. Das and Motilal Nehru   3. Jyotiba Phule
questions.exp: Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society (1905), Das and Motilal Nehru the Swaraj Party (1923), Phule the Satyashodhak Samaj (1873).

questions.q: Who is regarded as the Father of the Indian space programme?
questions.exp: Vikram Sarabhai founded ISRO's precursor INCOSPAR; Bhabha is father of the nuclear programme.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of electric charge?
questions.exp: Electric charge is measured in coulomb (1 C = 1 A x 1 s); ampere is the unit of current.

questions.q: The book 'Wings of Fire' is the autobiography of
questions.exp: 'Wings of Fire' (1999) was written by A. P. J. Abdul Kalam with Arun Tiwari.

questions.q: Mother Teresa was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in which year?
questions.exp: Mother Teresa received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979 for her humanitarian work.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Right under Part III of the Constitution?
questions.exp: The 44th Amendment (1978) removed the right to property from Part III; it is now a legal right under Article 300A.
